note: The one thing that makes a person theirs. Original writing for Pathfinder GM (2026-09-25). A quirk is a FRAME with slots: {small} a pocketable thing, {tool} a thing of their own trade (their occupation's objects), {food}, {animal}, {occasion}. A frame may declare: needs (body tags that must be true: hands, hair, gap_tooth, limp, burned_hand, scar_brow), requires (at least one of these tags already rolled), forbids (none of these). Frames are drawn WITHOUT REPLACEMENT within a settlement, so no two people in a town share one until the bag empties. Habits and fascinations only, by the user's ruling of 2026-09-25: no disability, illness, tic, phobia or addiction is a quirk; bodies keep their own marks.

frames.text: turns {small} over and over in their fingers whenever {occasion}
counts quietly under their breath whenever {occasion}
straightens {tool} whenever {occasion}
talks to {animal} as though they might answer
hums the same four notes whenever {occasion}
has a name for every one of {animal} and uses it
keeps {small} in a pocket and touches it whenever {occasion}
salutes out of old habit whenever {occasion}
whistles through the gap in their teeth whenever {occasion}
quotes an old proverb, slightly wrong, whenever {occasion}
offers {food} to anybody they talk to for long
polishes {tool} whenever {occasion}
taps the side of their nose knowingly whenever {occasion}
laughs a beat too late at every joke, but always laughs
calls everybody by their trade instead of their name — "morning, cooper"
keeps a running tally of favours owed, out loud
will not sit anywhere with their back to a door
smooths their hair flat whenever {occasion}
runs a thumb along the scar through their eyebrow whenever {occasion}
rubs the old burn on the back of their hand whenever {occasion}
swears their bad leg knows the weather a day before the sky does
pays in exact coin, always, and will not take change
sniffs {food} carefully before eating anything at all
carries {small} for luck and will not say who gave it to them
draws small circles with a fingertip on any table they sit at
says a word to the gods under their breath whenever {occasion}
spits over their left shoulder whenever {occasion}
folds any loose scrap of paper into a little bird and leaves it behind
goes up on their toes to see over people whenever {occasion}
compares everything to the way it was done in their home village
gives everybody a nickname within a minute of meeting them
never says goodbye — simply turns and leaves when they are done
glances at the sky whenever {occasion}
cracks their knuckles one at a time whenever {occasion}
can tell the hour by what the street smells of, and is never wrong
keeps every small thing anybody has ever given them, down to {small}
wears something yellow every single day and will not say why
shakes hands twice, as if the first did not count
sketches faces on scraps of anything whenever {occasion}
measures things against their thumb whenever {occasion}
tucks {food} into a pocket for later, every time it is offered
repeats the last word anybody says to them, thoughtfully, before answering
bows far too low to everyone, children included
sighs as if the world were a trial whenever {occasion}
has given {tool} a name and talks about it as a colleague

small: a folded letter gone soft at the creases
a key that opens nothing they own
a ring too small to wear

occasions.text: a bell rings anywhere in earshot
somebody from out of town speaks to them
